blocks.title: What is Microsoft Office?
rows: A productivity suite from Microsoft for documents, spreadsheets, presentations and other office work.
A collection of related productivity applications.

blocks.title: How Office first appeared
items: Bill Gates announced the Office suite
First commercial package, for Apple Macintosh
Office for Windows followed

blocks.title: Announcement is not release
blocks.text: The announcement came in **1988**; the first release (for the Apple Macintosh, not Windows) came in **1989**; the Windows version arrived in **1990**.

Office was built by teams at Microsoft. Bill Gates announced it and is Microsoft's co-founder, but he was not its sole creator. In basic exam questions, Office 1.0 is the introductory version designation.
Office = application software + a proprietary office suite. It is closed source, not open source.

blocks.title: Office versions to recognise
rows: Office 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 and 4.0 (numbering differed between Windows and Mac)

blocks.title: Handy points
items: Office 2021 was released in 2021.
Office for Mac 2011 was a real product.
Office 2021 was not the final Office release: Office 2024 followed.
Office 2019 and Office 2021 were one-time purchase editions.

blocks.title: There is no Office Vista
blocks.text: **Office Vista** is not a recognised Office release. Windows Vista was an operating system, not an Office edition.

blocks.title: Office applications at a glance
rows: Word processing: create, edit and format letters, reports and other documents
Spreadsheets: organise data, calculate with formulas, analyse information and build charts
Presentations: combine slides, text, images, audio and video
Record and organise digital notes, ideas and information

blocks.title: Access in more detail
items: Tables store records.
Relationships connect data.
Queries retrieve information.
Forms simplify data entry.
Reports organise output.
It is available on Windows in eligible editions and plans.

blocks.text: **Outlook** helps you organise contacts, calendars, appointments and meetings, besides handling email.

blocks.title: One-word memory
blocks.text: Word = documents, Excel = calculations, PowerPoint = presentations, Access = databases, Outlook = email, OneNote = notes.

sections.title: Legacy Tools and Other Exam Facts

blocks.title: Legacy Office tools
rows: Desktop publishing for newsletters, business cards, flyers, greeting cards and postcards. Retired from Microsoft 365 in October 2026; perpetual-edition support ended on 13 October 2026.
Organises pictures and makes basic image adjustments. It replaced Photo Editor in Office 2003; it was a replacement, not simply a new name.

blocks.title: Other exam facts
rows: A Windows drawing and basic image-editing application. It was not an original Office component.
**Microsoft Office Specialist**: a certification that shows practical Office skills through the relevant examinations.

blocks.title: Original package
blocks.text: The original core package was Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Both Paint and Outlook were absent from it, so a question that lists both as options has more than one valid answer.

blocks.title: Timeline
items: Office 365 announced and entered early testing.
28 June 2011
Commercial launch of Office 365.
Microsoft introduced the Microsoft 365 brand for business offerings. The original business bundle combined Office 365, Windows and enterprise security services.
21 April 2020
Several consumer and business subscriptions adopted Microsoft 365 names.

blocks.text: Some Office 365 plan names remained after 2020. The change did not rename every offering.

blocks.title: What Microsoft 365 provides
rows: Productivity applications, collaboration tools and cloud services.
Home users, educational institutions, businesses and large organisations.
Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote.

blocks.title: Plans and access
items: Personal plan: one person.
Family plan: up to six people in total, including the subscription owner.
Business and enterprise offerings serve organisational needs.
Apps and services vary by plan; do not assume every plan includes every desktop application.
Access is a Windows application in eligible plans.

blocks.title: Web and desktop
items: Word, Excel and PowerPoint for the web run in a browser.
Web apps are updated continuously and are not labelled as a fixed 2016, 2019 or 2021 edition.
Eligible subscriptions include installed desktop apps that can work offline.
The internet is needed for activation, updates and online services.

blocks.text: Microsoft 365 includes cloud services and eligible offline desktop apps; it is not online-only.

blocks.title: Microsoft 365 services
rows: Personal cloud files: store, synchronise and share files online
Shared content: organisational sites, shared document libraries and content management
Chats, online meetings and video conferencing, with shared work and document access
AI assistance inside supported Microsoft applications
Business analytics: connect to data and build interactive reports and dashboards

blocks.title: OneDrive vs SharePoint
items: OneDrive usually holds an individual's work files; SharePoint commonly holds shared team content.
Both support file sharing and collaboration.
OneDrive is a common cloud-saving location for Microsoft 365 documents, but local saving is also possible, so it is not compulsory for every document.
Files can be reached across supported devices with the required account and permissions.

blocks.title: Name check
blocks.text: The correct product name is **Teams**, not Team.

blocks.title: Plan limits and security
items: Copilot availability and usage limits depend on the plan.
Power BI publishing and sharing depend on licensing, and it is not automatically included in every Microsoft 365 subscription.
Security can include account authentication, multi-factor authentication and file-sharing controls; exact protection varies by service and subscription.

blocks.title: Working together
items: Supported apps allow real-time co-authoring.
Cloud files can be reached from different places over the internet.
Supported computers, tablets and smartphones give access, with platform differences.
Subscription apps get ongoing updates; automatic installation depends on settings and policy.

blocks.title: Quick match
blocks.text: OneDrive = cloud files, SharePoint = shared content, Teams = meetings, Power BI = dashboards, Copilot = AI help.

blocks.title: Office 2024 overview
items: Consumer editions became available on 1 October 2024.
It succeeds Office 2021 and was the current perpetual Office generation as checked in October 2026.
It is a one-time purchase, without a recurring Microsoft 365 subscription.
It is available for supported Windows PCs and Macs.

blocks.title: Office 2024 editions
rows: Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote for one PC or Mac
Designed for commercial and government deployment needs

blocks.title: New look and features
rows: A refreshed default theme gives applications a consistent appearance and fits Windows 11. Retail Office 2021 also got a visual refresh; LTSC 2021 did not.
Excel 2024 charts can reference dynamic arrays and adjust when the linked array recalculates and changes size. Excel 2021 already supported dynamic arrays; the 2024 improvement concerns charts.
Place a live camera feed directly on a slide and apply formatting, styles and effects to the camera object.

blocks.title: Purchase and support
items: Office 2024 keeps the feature set you bought and receives security and quality updates.
A later major Office edition normally needs a separate purchase.
Microsoft 365 gets ongoing feature upgrades while you stay subscribed.
Both editions launched with roughly five years of support; 2024 has the later end date.

blocks.text: Office 2024 = one-time purchase. Microsoft 365 = subscription. Cameo = live camera on slides.
The correct Apple presentation app is **Keynote**, not Keynotes.

blocks.title: Development and licensing
rows: Free and open source, built by a worldwide community and supported by **The Document Foundation**, a nonprofit organisation. It grew out of the OpenOffice.org codebase but is a separate project.
Pages, Numbers and Keynote offer free core functions; some premium features need payment.
Business plans of Google Workspace are generally paid; consumer Docs, Sheets and Slides have free-access options.

blocks.title: LibreOffice: six components
rows: Databases, tables, queries, forms and reports.
Editing and displaying mathematical formulas and equations.

blocks.text: Math is not a calculation engine. Use **Calc** for spreadsheet calculations.

blocks.title: Version facts
items: LibreOffice 7.4 Community was released. It is a historical release, not the current latest version.
The official download page showed LibreOffice 26.8.1 on this check date.

blocks.title: Memory line
blocks.text: Writer = words, Calc = calculations, Impress = slides, Draw = diagrams, Base = database, Math = equations.

blocks.title: Microsoft Word: early development
rows: Word was initially known as **Multi-Tool Word**.
Its early release history dates to 1983.
**Charles Simonyi** and **Richard Brodie** played central roles at Microsoft. Brodie wrote much of the original program, with input from Simonyi and other developers.

blocks.text: Keep the individual developers separate from Microsoft, the company behind the product.

blocks.title: LinkedIn and Microsoft
rows: A professional networking platform for career connections, profiles and recruitment.
Microsoft acquired LinkedIn in **2016**; the deal was completed on 8 December 2016.

blocks.title: Correcting common exam traps
items: First Office platform: Apple Macintosh, not Windows.
Announcement in 1988 is different from the Mac release in 1989.
Original core package: Word, Excel and PowerPoint.
Paint and Outlook were both absent from the original package.
Office for Mac 2011 existed and is not a fictitious version.
Office 2021 was not the final Office release; Office 2024 followed.
Office 2019 and 2021 were one-time purchase editions.
Microsoft 365 includes cloud services and eligible offline apps; it is not online-only.
Office is proprietary and closed source, not open source.

blocks.title: Programming-language questions
blocks.text: Office and Microsoft 365 contain many applications and services. A precise language answer must name the component, so do not treat a short list such as C++ and C# as a full description of the whole product family.

revision: Microsoft Office is a proprietary, closed-source productivity suite and counts as application software.
Bill Gates announced Office in 1988; first Mac release 1989; first Windows release 1990.
Original core applications: Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Paint and Outlook were not in the original package.
Word = documents, Excel = spreadsheets, PowerPoint = presentations, Access = databases, Outlook = email, OneNote = notes.
Office Vista does not exist; Office for Mac 2011 was real; Picture Manager replaced Photo Editor in Office 2003.
MOS = Microsoft Office Specialist, a certification of practical Office skills.
Office 365: tested in 2010, commercial launch 28 June 2011; Microsoft 365 business brand in 2017; plan renaming on 21 April 2020.
Microsoft 365 is a paid subscription with cloud services and offline desktop apps; Family plan covers up to six people.
OneDrive = personal cloud files; SharePoint = shared content; Teams = meetings (not Team); Power BI = dashboards; Copilot = AI help.
Office 2024: consumer release on 1 October 2024, one-time purchase, support ends October 2029; Office 2021 support ended October 2026.
Office 2024 highlights: Fluent design, Excel charts with dynamic arrays and PowerPoint Cameo (live camera on a slide).
Equivalents: Writer, Calc, Impress (LibreOffice); Pages, Numbers, Keynote (Apple); Docs, Sheets, Slides (Google).
LibreOffice is free and open source (The Document Foundation) with six parts: Writer, Calc, Impress, Draw, Base, Math.
LibreOffice 7.4 Community was released on 18 August 2022.
Word was first called Multi-Tool Word; developers Charles Simonyi and Richard Brodie; history from 1983.
Microsoft acquired LinkedIn in 2016; the deal completed on 8 December 2016.
